interpretations.rationale: Witnessed and bounded, now with a second producer recorded and with the suffix route partly executed. The trim witness stands: with recorded accepted indexes drifted to 10, 9 and 7 over six indices of content and every node's decided report at 9, trim(None) returned no error and compacted index 7, past the leader's own content, after which its reads of indices 5 and 6 reported Trimmed (ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a events 9-15). The discriminator this question carried asked whether a producer other than trim can raise a compacted index past a replica's content, and the snapshot receipt answers that it can: with the same drifted state, snapshot(Some(8), false) returned Ok, advanced the leader's compacted index to 8 and produced a snapshot holding none of the five decided entries (e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c events 0-5). That second producer is stricter in one respect and looser in another than trim: it needs no recorded accepted index at all - its bound is the leader's decided index - so a drift confined to the decided index would be enough for it, while trim additionally needs the drifted value to be the configuration's minimum recorded accepted index. What remains bounded from the earlier reading: both producers are bounded by values the leader derives for itself, so a replica whose recorded report is still truthful keeps trim's bound honest (the minimum), and the snapshot witness also required the leader's own decided index to have drifted. Correction review: the drift knowledge this account cites was narrowed to revision 2, which keeps the half this account needs - the reported accepted index drifts one further index per re-synchronization round, inflating exactly the recorded accepted indexes the trim bound is derived from - and bounds the decided index to the rounds in which a write quorum of drifted reports covers it; this account never assumes the decided index keeps following the drift, since it reads the decided values from its own receipt's samples (every node at 9), so the narrowing leaves its conclusion unchanged and the knowledge use is re-read at revision 2 below. The suffix route is now partly executed: in the snapshot-capable sibling case the lagging replica re-synchronized below the leader's compacted index (the leader had compacted to 8 with a snapshot holding zero ids) was not refused and did not panic - it received that complete snapshot and no suffix, reported accepted 10 / decided 10 and read two decided entries where the configuration decided six (0b9c22ae5fb043588aa7efa3ad009b25 events 152-162). On that route the outcome is therefore a silently empty snapshot rather than an error or an abort, while the abort the drift lineage did produce comes from a different entry point, the public snapshot call on a NoSnapshot instance (40ab66a5c5c847619ae2ff68b85641e7-question-1). The routes this question names as alternatives - a direct range read and a store-level trim below a compacted index - remain unexecuted.

knowledge.assertion: trim accepted a drifted bound and compacted past the content the leader held
the snapshot path accepted a drifted bound and produced a snapshot holding none of the entries
trim's bound is the minimum recorded accepted index, so a truthful replica keeps it honest
the reported accepted index drifts one index per re-synchronization round while the decided index follows only while a write quorum covers it

counterevidence: Every node's decided report had also drifted to 9, so the documented all-decided precondition was satisfied only in the drifted bookkeeping; the obligation I rely on is that the compacted index must not exceed the entries the leader holds, which it did (7 for trim, 8 for the snapshot).
The trim call returned Ok, so nothing in its own result signals the over-compaction; the witness is the compacted index together with the content sampled before and after.

The in-cluster route below a compacted index is now executed rather than argued, and it does not abort: the lagging replica was re-synchronized with a complete but empty snapshot and a shortened decided log (0b9c22ae5fb043588aa7efa3ad009b25 events 161, 162), so the over-compaction of this account leads to a silent loss on a lagging replica; the abort seen in the same lineage belongs to the public snapshot call on a NoSnapshot instance and is recorded under its own question.
limitations: The trim over-compaction is bounded to replicas whose recorded accepted index has drifted; a truthful replica would have kept the bound lower.

The underflow remainder is a property of a storage or caller that requests a prefix below the compacted index by a route other than the cluster's own log syncs: a direct range read and a store-level trim below a compacted index remain unexecuted, other storage implementations may differ, and the trait leaves out-of-range behaviour to the implementer. The abort observed in this lineage came from the NoSnapshot snapshot-call path, not from this remainder.
The baseline comparisons of both receipts are unknown because they were admitted through event names shared across cases in one execution; those states are asserted from the sampled operands.

One three-node configuration, three reconnection rounds, one leader change for trim and one snapshot-capable entry type were exercised; the peers that receive a forwarded compaction were not sampled beyond their accepted and decided indexes, and the lagging-replica outcome was observed with the leader's log empty above its compacted index.

For the trim path the observed over-compaction is the minimum of the drifted recorded values, so the number of indices it passes beyond the leader's content depends on how many rounds each replica drifted; only one such combination was sampled.

interpretations.rationale: Witnessed, with the discriminator's variants settled one further step by an executed sibling case. Witness: with the drift in place (accepted 9, 9 and 6, decided 9, six indices of content), snapshot(Some(8), false) returned Ok on the leader, its compacted index became 8, and the snapshot reachable at index 0 held zero entry ids where the log had five decided entries (e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c events 0-5); the comparisons requiring the compacted index to reach six and the snapshot to hold five entries were violated at the call event. Variants: (i) a request equal to the drifted decided index is not protected, because the equal case maps it to the decided log without the StopSign (8) which still exceeds the content (6) - this corrects my earlier counter-argument; (ii) the bound is computed on whichever node receives the call, so a follower with the same drifted decided index accepts the same request, and the local_only flag only decides whether the request is forwarded; (iii) the forwarded form repeats the derivation on every peer - each peer's own snapshot call compares the requested index against its own decided index (which in the observed run was also 9) and builds from its own range, so the peers end in the same loss rather than a different state, while the sampling here covered only their accepted and decided indexes (events 4, 5); (iv) the form the loss takes is whatever the entry type's Snapshot::create gives to an empty slice, which for this entry type is an empty snapshot that the reads then report for the compacted region. The lagging-replica variant is now executed in a sibling case: after the leader change the new leader compacted inside its drifted decided index with a snapshot holding zero ids (compacted 8), and the replica whose reported accepted index lay below that compacted index was re-synchronized without any error or abort, receiving that complete snapshot and no suffix, after which it reported accepted 10 / decided 10 and read two decided entries where six were decided (0b9c22ae5fb043588aa7efa3ad009b25 events 152-162, event 162 recording panicked false) - the loss takes the form of variant (iv), an installed empty snapshot, and the same exchange moved the leader's decided index to 10. Correction review: the drift knowledge this account cites was narrowed to revision 2 (the reported accepted index still drifts one further index per round, and the decided index follows while a write quorum covers it); this account needs only that the leader's decided index can exceed the entries it holds, which its own receipt samples directly (decided 9 over six indices of content), so the narrowing leaves the conclusion unchanged and the use is re-read at revision 2 below.

ebbec352695d43beb398bb1b239cda41-gap-7.explanation: The correction does not reach this account. What it needs from the drift knowledge is that a re-synchronization can raise the reported accepted index, and that a leader then adopts a decided index above the entries it holds; the narrowed revision 2 still states that the accepted index drifts one index per round and that the decided index follows while a write quorum covers it, and this account's own receipt samples the exceeding decided index directly (decided 9 against six indices of content at e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c events 0-5). The witness, the equal-index correction and the derivation-based variants therefore stand, and the knowledge use is re-read at revision 2.

knowledge.assertion: the snapshot bound comes from the decided index alone
the snapshot path accepted a drifted bound and produced a snapshot holding none of the entries
a replica re-synchronized below the compacted index receives a complete snapshot built from the empty range
the reported accepted index drifts one index per re-synchronization round while the decided index follows only while a write quorum covers it

counterevidence: The call itself returned Ok, so nothing in its result signals the loss; the witness is the compacted index together with the number of entries the produced snapshot holds.
The user supplied the index 8; the documented note allows any index up to the decided index, which was 9, so the request was inside the documented allowance rather than a caller error.
The apparent protection offered by the equal case does not hold in the observed state: it lowers the bound from 9 to 8, which is still above the content (6).

The loss on a lagging replica is silent rather than fatal: the executed sibling case raised no panic and returned no error, so a replica that reads the decided log afterwards sees a shortened log represented by an empty snapshot (0b9c22ae5fb043588aa7efa3ad009b25 events 161, 162).
limitations: The consequence depends on the entry type's snapshot: here the snapshot records its input entries and is empty for an empty slice; an entry type that reconstructs state differently could behave differently.

The peers that receive the forwarded compaction were not sampled in any run, so that variant is still read from the derivation that each peer computes its own bound and range; the lagging-replica variant is now executed, and the follower-side and equal-index variants remain argued from the derivation and from the bound arithmetic.

One three-node configuration, three reconnection rounds, one leader change, one index and two entry types (one without snapshots, one with) were exercised, and the comparisons tying the before and after samples to their admissions are unknown because of a shared event name in the same execution, so those states are asserted from the sampled operands (e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c events 0-5).

The over-compaction was produced through the drift; no run established what the same call does when the decided index is truthful and another replica is simply behind, which would need a lagging replica without any drift.
